subject: Re: Mid-term capacity change and VAT handling - ZenPharm
raw_messages:
From: Sasha Novak <sasha.novak@zenpharm.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: ZenPharm Billing <billing@zenpharm.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Jul 2025 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Mid-cycle capacity bump — proration & VAT question

Hi Karthik,

Quick one from finance — we need to bump our Dedicated capacity by 6 GPUs effective immediately (start date 2025-07-10). Our contract renews on 2025-09-01. Can you confirm how Redwood will invoice us for the remaining partial period? Specifically:

- Will we get a prorated charge for the 7/10–9/01 period or a credit/adjustment on the next invoice?
- How will EU VAT be handled? We are based in Germany (ZenPharm GmbH) and I think this is a B2B supply. Do you need our VAT registration number?

I attached our current contract for reference (current_contract.pdf).

Thanks — if it's easier, we can do a quick call this afternoon.

Best,
Sasha Novak
Head of Cloud Ops
ZenPharm GmbH

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sasha Novak <sasha.novak@zenpharm.com>
Cc: ZenPharm Billing <billing@zenpharm.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Jul 2025 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid-cycle capacity bump — proration & VAT question

Hi Sasha — thanks for the heads up and for attaching the contract. Short answers below and a proposed next step.

Summary (high-level):
- Proration: We prorate on a daily basis for Dedicated capacity upgrades. You can choose: 1) an immediate charge for the prorated amount invoiced today, or 2) a credit applied to your next invoice (we typically apply credits at the next billing cycle).
- VAT: For EU B2B customers with a valid VAT ID, we invoice at 0% VAT and include the VAT ID + reverse-charge note. If no VAT ID is provided, we will apply German VAT at the standard rate.

I put together a quick estimate with the two billing options and the prorated calculation in the attached spreadsheet (proration_estimate_zenpharm.xlsx). The estimate assumes a 6 GPU top-up on 2025-07-10 and prorates to 2025-09-01; it includes a line for the Dedicated monthly unit price and the per-GPU add-on.

What I need from you to finalize:
1) Confirm whether you want an immediate invoice or a credit applied to the Sep 1 invoice.
2) Share your VAT registration number if you have one (we'll apply reverse charge if valid).
3) If purchasing requires a PO, please attach it so we can include the PO number on the invoice.

If it's helpful, we can issue a draft invoice (PDF) for your review before charging.

Cheers,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0192

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Jul 2025 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid-cycle capacity bump — VAT & proration guidance (internal)

Karthik / Ben — quick finance note to include in the customer response:

- VAT treatment: If ZenPharm provides a valid EU VAT ID and confirms this is a B2B purchase, we should apply reverse charge (0% VAT) and include the standard reverse-charge wording on the invoice plus their VAT ID. If they do not provide a VAT ID, apply DE VAT (19%).
- Invoicing flow: For Dedicated capacity mid-cycle increases we usually:
  * Option A: Raise an immediate pro-rated invoice for the remainder of the billing period. Use invoice code RC-PRORATE and include PO if provided.
  * Option B: Raise a small interim invoice for the pro-rated portion and then consolidate on the Sep 1 invoice (this is option A split across docs — pick one).
- Accounting note: If they want net-zero VAT we need to capture their VAT ID and save the validation screenshot in the billing ticket.

Attaching our internal VAT guidance snippet (VAT_guidance_internal.pdf).

-Marissa
VP, Finance Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sasha Novak <sasha.novak@zenpharm.com>
Cc: ZenPharm Billing <billing@zenpharm.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Jul 2025 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid-cycle capacity bump — proration & VAT question

Hi Sasha — attached is a draft invoice and the proration worksheet for transparency (invoice_draft_zn5561.pdf, proration_estimate_zenpharm.xlsx). Quick summary of the numbers (assuming reverse charge / valid VAT ID):

Proration window: 2025-07-10 to 2025-09-01 (53 days)
Monthly Dedicated unit price: EUR 6,000 / GPU
Prorated per-GPU charge: (6,000 * 53/31) — note we prorate by days in the billing cycle; the attached calc shows the line-by-line math.
Estimated prorated charge (6 GPUs): EUR 6,000 * 6 * (53/62) = EUR 30,968.71 (example; see sheet for rounding).
VAT treatment: Assuming you supply a valid EU VAT ID, invoice will be issued at 0% VAT with reverse-charge wording. If you cannot supply a VAT ID, an additional 19% DE VAT will be applied to the invoice total.

Options to proceed:
1) Issue immediate pro-rated invoice and collect payment now (preferred by finance for cash visibility). We can send a DocuSign/payable link and mark the invoice with your PO.
2) Apply the prorated amount as a credit to your Sep 1 invoice (no charge now).

Next steps from your side: VAT ID + PO number + preferred billing option. If you want the immediate invoice, I can issue it today and share the payment link.

Best,
Karthik

From: Sasha Novak <sasha.novak@zenpharm.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: ZenPharm Billing <billing@zenpharm.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jul 2025 16:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid-cycle capacity bump — proration & VAT question

Hi Karthik — thanks for the clear breakdown and the draft. Apologies for the delay — finance was verifying the VAT details.

Confirmation:
- We are ZenPharm GmbH, VAT DE123456789 (attached PO-9873.pdf).
- Please proceed with Option 1 (immediate pro-rated invoice). Include our PO number on the invoice.
- We expect to pay the invoice within standard 30 days.

If you can send the invoice PDF and the payment link, I'll route it to our accounts payable and confirm once payment is initiated.

Thanks again — and happy to hop on a short call if any of the invoice metadata needs adjustment.

Cheers,
Sasha
